text:
rita: Noticed a weird thing on the latency page: p50 for /v1/respond is slightly higher than p95 for some client slices. dashboard shows p50=320ms, p95=300ms, p99=860ms.
noah: That usually means sample bias or different measurement points. Are we mixing client-side timings with server-side?
rita: I pulled the raw series with the internal API: GET /telemetry/latency?endpoint=/v1/respond&quantiles=0.5,0.95,0.99&group_by=client_region
alex: Do you have sample counts? small N can invert quantiles.
rita: For eu-north slice sample_count=18, p50=320, p95=300, p99=860.
priya: With N=18 p95 calculation is noisy. Also check for retry/chained calls: if some clients hit preflight that we exclude from p95 but include in p50, shapes flip.
metrics-bot: metrics-bot: note added: metric_series_id=ms-99321, last_ingest=2026-03-22T09:34:10Z, tags=[measurement_point:request_start].
noah: measurement_point tag is the key. Our console has historically displayed whichever measurement_point was present first for a route. That causes mixes when different SDKs emit different points.
alex: Proposal: telemetry API returns quantiles plus per-quantile metadata: sample_count_pXX and measurement_point_pXX so UIs can group by consistent measurement points.
priya: I like returning measurement_point_pXX. Alternatively, require a measurement_point query param so the backend normalizes series before computing quantiles. Which is less invasive?
rita: Requiring measurement_point param would break many ad-hoc queries. Better: compute quantiles per measurement_point and expose them as separate rows in the response. Then console can choose which row to surface by default (we pick 'server_generate_start').
noah: Implementation detail: compute counts and also a simple confidence estimate (bootstrapped CI or asymptotic stderr). Even a rough ci_low/ci_high helps.
alex: UI idea: when sample_count_p99 < 50 show an inline caution: "low-sample tail; consider filtering measurement_point or increasing window". Also show which measurement_point that quantile used.
priya: Alerting change: update p95-based SLOs to only evaluate when sample_count_p95 >= 200 for tenant-level alerts. Otherwise we'll get noisy signals on small cohorts.
rita: Also found the root cause for eu-north: a routing change last night added a transient fallback that routes a tiny percentage to legacy-pool. Legacy-pool has longer cold-starts; that explains the p99 tail.
noah: Can console surface route_reason like fallback=fallback-disk-cache? If telemetry returns route_policy and route_reason tags that would make troubleshooting faster.
alex: Yes, add route_policy and route_reason into the per-quantile row metadata. We already tag traces with route_reason; we can wire that into the metrics pipeline but need to be careful with tag cardinality.
priya: Cardinality guard: only allowed values from a controlled enum, not free text. We'll maintain route_reason enum in routing-service.
metrics-bot: metrics-bot: scheduled job: compute per-measurement-point quantiles hourly for last 1h,6h,24h windows.
rita: OK next steps action list: 1) backend: compute quantiles grouped by measurement_point + attach sample_count_pXX + ci_pXX + route_policy/route_reason (enum). 2) console: surface measurement_point and show low-sample stripe + tooltip. 3) alerting: add sample_count threshold for tenant SLOs.
noah: I'll open a telemetry API RFC with sample response schema and breaking-change mitigation plan.
alex: I'll prototype UI mock and add the low-sample annotation.
priya: I'll update routing-service to prefer warming fallback pool or reduce fallback percentage for small-client cohorts.
rita: Thanks team. Let's review RFC tomorrow. If canary shows persistent p99 tied to legacy-pool we'll trigger an emergency hotfix. :warning:
